Long-term Memory

Extend deep agents with persistent memory across threads.

Deep agents come with a local filesystem to offload memory. By default, this filesystem is stored in agent state and is transient to a single thread—files are lost when the conversation ends.

You can extend deep agents with long-term memory by using a CompositeBackend that routes specific paths to persistent storage. This enables hybrid storage where some files persist across threads while others remain ephemeral.

graph LR %% Main Entry DA[Deep Agent] --> PR{Path Router} %% Routing Paths PR -->|/memories/*| SB[Store Backend] PR -->|other| StB[State Backend] %% Final Persistence Layer SB --> P[(Persistent
across threads)] StB --> E[(Ephemeral
single thread)] %% Styling for better readability style PR fill:#333,stroke:#fff style P fill:#222,stroke:#aaa style E fill:#222,stroke:#aaa

Setup

Use a CompositeBackend to combine ephemeral and persistent storage.

from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from deepagents.backends import CompositeBackend, StateBackend, StoreBackend
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore

def make_backend(runtime):
    return CompositeBackend(
        default=StateBackend(runtime), # Ephemeral
        routes={
            "/memories/": StoreBackend(runtime) # Persistent
        }
    )

agent = create_deep_agent(
    store=InMemoryStore(),
    backend=make_backend
)

How it works

Short-term (transient) filesystem

  • Stored in agent state via StateBackend.
  • Persists only within the current thread.
  • e.g., /notes.txt

Long-term (persistent) filesystem

  • Stored in LangGraph Store via StoreBackend.
  • Persists across all threads and conversations.
  • Accessed via routed paths, e.g., /memories/preferences.txt.

Cross-thread Persistence

Agents in different threads can share knowledge by reading/writing to the persistent paths.

# Thread 1
agent.invoke({
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Save my preferences to /memories/prefs.txt"}]
}, config=config1)

# Thread 2
agent.invoke({
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Read my preferences"}]
}, config=config2) # Can read /memories/prefs.txt

Store Implementations

InMemoryStore (Development)

Great for quick iteration and testing. Data is lost when the process restarts.

from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore
store = InMemoryStore()

PostgresStore (Production)

Use for persistent storage in production environments.

from langgraph.store.postgres import PostgresStore
import os

store_ctx = PostgresStore.from_conn_string(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])
store = store_ctx.__enter__()
store.setup()

Use Cases

User Preferences

Save user settings to remember them across conversations.

system_prompt="""
When users tell you their preferences, save them to /memories/user_preferences.txt
so you remember them in future conversations.
"""

Self-improving Instructions

Update system behavior based on feedback.

system_prompt="""
You have a file at /memories/instructions.txt with additional instructions.
When users provide feedback, update this file using edit_file.
"""

Knowledge Base

Accumulate facts over time.

# Conv 1: Learn about project
"We're building a React app. Save notes." -> writes to /memories/project_notes.txt

# Conv 2: Recall info
"What framework?" -> reads /memories/project_notes.txt

Best Practices

  • Use descriptive paths: e.g., /memories/research/topic_a/sources.txt instead of /memories/file1.txt.
  • Document structure: Tell the agent about the file structure in the system prompt.
  • Prune old data: Instruct the agent to delete or archive old files to keep retrieval efficient.
  • Choose right storage: InMemoryStore for dev, PostgresStore for prod. Name-space by assistant_id for multi-tenant apps.
